Author: @Volkaroar
Content:
I think what really appeals to me the most about this channel is actually not the content itself, but the commentary between two best...friends? lmao, the conversations and nostalgic stories that Ken and Dane have on here in between the content topic feels like friends getting together to discuss past times and memories is nice and wholesome. It's entertaining, knowing nothing about you both, that we feel like we can relate to you in some ways and really just listen in. 

With that said, I think with new content ideas you have to just let it foster and grow. They won't pick up too much because regular channel viewers and subscribers are here for the content you've done a lot of but the new content videos (psychics, cop stuff, judge mathis, etc.) will draw in new people not familiar with your current audience content and get to watch and enjoy those as well. I would probably say invest like 80% of your time in what the analytics say, but increase new content and just let it grow. You could introduce new things like life fail topics (serious blunders made on videos, or pranks), natural disaster content, or even take it old school and play card/board games somehow to lean back on that nostalgic image (great potential branding opportunities on top of just having fun). If not playing video games, then possibly just talk commentary about certain games as a better tie in to the toastygames channel to link the two together. 

As for the branding with other up and coming youtubers to your other business, you would probably be in the best position to do masterclasses and charge for that time. Anyone who looks at what you've been able to accomplish and really understand the industry of streaming and takes it seriously would see the value in the charge and go for that. You all have a sense of being genuine and real, which is to your credit for others who try to superimpose that authenticity that comes so naturally for you. 

Just some thoughts on my end, as a repeat viewer of your content for some time now. Thanks for the videos and entertainment, and I hope you all have some happy holidays! See you in 2025!

Author: @WeAreTheGemini
Content:
I'm so happy to see you guys are doing well and are happy! I love your videos and have been a fan since the early days! Seeing you feeling more positive about where you're at gives me so much joy. Been binging the videos for the past two days, and you never disappoint. The realness you bring to some of the most ridiculous and dark aspects of the human experience and stuff that happens in the world, really such a positive impact, and always super entertaining. The chemistry with you and Buff is gold. 

As for what I would like to see more of, I always love the colab videos you do with other YouTubers, as special features - I would love to see a video with Dane and Felix along with Ken reacting to some of the crazy videos together, not sure what the chemistry would be like, but it would be great to see that. Would be like the golden trio! I'm not sure if you've done that before, I might have missed it somehow, but yeah. Just generally some of the stuff you guys talk about, sharing your experiences and telling stories, making each other laugh with your differences, kind of reminds me of like a buddy cop movie, or like Odd Couple. Sharing little tidbits where the video you guys are watching becomes like background to the interaction you're having with one another. Such a unique niche you guys have here. Always interesting to hear your stories and what it was like growing up in USA and the South. Ken, the way you see the world is super interesting, man. And the interaction between you and Buff is what really brings it out and makes you shine, bro. Buff is just such a ray of sunshine. Thank you for your laugh, bro. 

Some of the stuff I would like to see less of? Just for me personally, I don't really vibe with some of the more grotesque videos and topics, not sure if that's too vague, because let's face it some of the stuff you react to gets pretty WILD! And people are super weird and get up to the most ridiculous things, but sometimes the series you do; like 600 Pound Life, I just didn't vibe with. It wasn't for me. Hopefully Kay's Cooking videos get over their nonsense and you guys can watch some more of that, but I mean, it is what it is. Not too keen about the drama videos, tbh or some of the reality shows are just junk TV. If that's a bit more specific, idk. (The Big Ed videos were alright, but sometimes got too much and trashy).

I think more of the stuff that pushes the boundaries and gets wild, but kind of makes you stop and think about how wild things can get, and makes you look at your own life and just be thankful that your own stuff isn't as crazy, like I guess that's what I like. Sense of humour, seeing the good in crazy things, the chats between you guys and going off topic just vibing, the laughter, the jokes, some life insights that you have, that's all good. Being real. Alright - that's a lot, but you asked for feedback and I only ever leave short comments, so I thought let me tell you now. haha. Here's hoping that 2025 will be even bigger and better for you guys. Merry Christmas, enjoy the break and stay Toasty, my friends!

In Britain, they sometimes call themselves "lawfull rebellion", after a clause from the draft version of the Magna Carta (that's from the year 1215, people!)

 This is a growing social phenomenon that is clogging up the courts with nonsense paperwork (paper terrorism) and taking up police time unnecessarily.  Their ideas are spread mostly by conmen who sell "information packages" which include instructions on how to make your own licence plate for your cart. There is some tazing in some of the traffic stops, but the big payoff is the window smashing, which can be as satisfying as a tazing

the Shrodinger's Cat channel is still up, even though the owner passed on 2 years ago.  It still has a lot of sovcit and 1st amendment auditors. videos.

Author: @sunstripe85
Content:
Btw I don't see an issue with brand deals, except when channels choose anything and everything including sketchy af products. But you haven't done that and most channels don't. I first learned of Raycon, for example, in a sponsored video and those things are awesome! They're so good my mom ended up wanting them too.

 I learn of a lot of interesting resources and products through YouTube sponsored videos, and if I see a particular company be mentioned on multiple channels I follow, i can usually get a good view on how "trustworthy" it may be based on who shills it and what they say and why. 

Obviously i still do research, and obviously there have been companies who lots of great, ethical channels recommended that later turned out to be sketchy companies-- but in those cases, it seems like most of the time the company was deliberately obfuscating things and the influencers either genuinely didn't know or ended up overlooking oddities due to financial needs

But overall I've had great luck with looking into and getting products or resources from channels i love, especially when i see that same thing talked about multiple places. Raycon is a great example, as are my Vessi shoes, and many other things i can't even think of offhand. Even the mobile games sometimes are a huge hit for me. I've become a loyal customer to some products for years because of YouTube sponsored ads, and it's not that i was duped or anything dumb like that.

On the contrary, sometimes it's hard to know what you can and can't trust online or whether reviews are AI influenced or bought or whatever on sites that are supposed to be neutral reviews. 

For me, having YouTubers I've followed for years talk about something means I tend to have a really good view of first of all whether I think the YouTuber is maybe actually using it or not which you can usually tell based on what they're saying in the ad. It's clear in some cases that the company has a very strict script they want followed because I see the same thing with only slight variations on multiple different channels. When I see that, personally, it gives me more pause than the ones where it seems like the creator is allowed to be a bit more personable. Especially if they're allowed to kind of mention even ....not faults or flaws or downsides per se (although it's awesome if they ever are), but rather where it doesn't seem like they're being forced to only talk about positive generic things. 

There are still times where I have tried something out and it didn't work out for me personally forever but frankly that's an incredibly small minority compared to the overall pretty high success rate I've had with YouTube sponsors. Because I'm very specific in what I pay attention to and I will do extra research and I don't even get the name of the company or whatever on my radar without it having come from some varying levels of trusted sources.

 It's basically like having something I can Google to find the best potential companies or products for XYZ reason, without having to go through a ton of different random compilation lists and try to figure out how much I trust or believe these source who wrote that list and whatever financial gain they may or may not have behind it etc. 

I know very clearly with YouTube sponsorships that the creator is getting paid for this so I always immediately take that into account as part of the context. And that doesn't mean it's a negative mark on the product, it just means I know that there's money involved in the background and so I will keep that in mind when I'm listening to the pitch for it and when I'm considering whether I think it could be something useful for me and whether I want to look into it or not. 

I also will sometimes later decide to try something that I remember hearing many YouTubers talk about, and if my favorite channels haven't done a sponsored add on it recently enough or I can't find it or whatever I will actually just search in the YouTube search for the name of that product and sponsorship or something.

 And then I can find coupon codes to use which is another really helpful aspect. 

Of course I always default first to the channels I like who actually introduced me to it but like I said sometimes it's been months or like a year since they did the sponsored ad on it and I've heard enough since then that I realized I really want to try it but the code the YouTuber I follow had no longer works. 

It's a little random but I imagine hopefully other people do the same thing so creators like you can even get some kick back from the links or codes from completely random YouTube viewers who maybe don't know you or maybe haven't watched that video fully but will use your code which hopefully gives you credit.

Author: @sunstripe85
Content:
5:26 personally, I really hope you DON'T go full commentary/drama/etc. I follow many great channels like that but you're the only one like you. I love that you have such a wide array of topics, and frankly I would have no idea whatsoever of so many shows out there (and subsequent memes) without you. I'm never watching any of the TLC shows, etc, but I will absolutely watch you and Dane talk about it. And that's the only way I  would ever even consider watching the shows themselves-- or even watching other channels cover that show or topic afterward. So the variety I love includes everything you're doing or mentioned, with the longer running themes like predator or cooking or etc, and the cop videos, and the random tv shows, and covering topical things like crazy Internet influencers. 

For me, it's exactly like you said-- like i get to sit on my couch with some friends watching silly or crazy or interesting stuff. 

I am subscribed to literally thousands of channels, but there's probably a couple hundred max that i regularly return to. I tend to get in the swing of watching certain topics a lot and then not others. So I'll get on an art kick where I'm watching all the art channels and videos for days or weeks or months, depending on my hyperfocus at the time, and then suddenly I'll be totally over art and start my BWC era or true crime or etc. 

There are VERY few channels i will still pop in on occasionally even in the midst of that obsession, if the channel doesn't fit the theme. 

You are literally one of the only channels i can even think of offhand that stands the test of time for me, and I'll randomly watch no matter my hyperfocus. 

I won't be as good about watching many of yours at once in those streaks but the fact that I will watch anything else is huge. You've even been a great transitional channel for me many times, where I'll know I'm ready to switch themes because i gravitate you binge watching lots of videos on your channel. 

It's like you're my perfect reset while also my favorite channel to just randomly watch. 

And then any time i watch one of your videos, there's a high likelihood i will binge all or most of the videos i missed since my last binge or since the last time i was in a themed hyperfocus that directly includes your channel.

The variety of your channel coupled with the ability to go from light hearted and funny to serious and respectful or interesting is very unique on YouTube if you ask me. 

I'll watch you no matter what, I'm sure, but if you were to convert to just commentary for example I know for me at least I would inevitably stop watching you as randomly because you would be straight in the commentary theme of my brain... So when I'm in that hyperfocus i would include you but when I'm not i wouldn't.

Not to mention what i like about the commentary channels i follow is their research and often detailed knowledge of the context and their commitment to following up with significant updates later on. 

That's just not usually how you guys roll -- which is not a bad thing. I love how refreshing it is to see people just react to whatever they want, and that you try to get some amount of context and will give what info you have but you're also very transparent about what you do and don't know or to what extent you've researched any of it. I love that because, again, it feels like chatting with friends about something and them relaying info they've heard but without being authoritative to the point that it doesn't invite questions or opinions. 

It's nice because it also means the comments can be more varied in view at times, which gives me more perspectives and context or further topics to explore than i would get in a channel that hasn't accrued such an eclectic audience. 

I would say the only issue i personally have is i watch YouTube almost exclusively on the YouTube Roku app which frankly is very limited and kind of awkward. 

I want to binge a bunch of your videos but it just randomly chooses other videos of yours to autoplay or it only lets me watch your latest video and go backwards. But then I'm seeing newer videos on a topic that may be part 5 or 3 or something, before i see 1 or 2. 

I will try to find your saved playlists if I'm really determined to learn about this specific topic, but sometimes you don't have a relevant playlist or you do but it's so huge that it takes awhile to be able to get to the right place to start where i need to. 

I don't know how hard it would be to create but I'd LOVE something along the lines of "Catch up with Ken (and Dane)" where either it's a section on your page with individual playlists of the topics you've covered in, say, the most recent 1-2 months or whatever, and each playlist is set so you can go there and see, say, any specific show you've covered. Like let's say you've covered a creepy milf show, and you started it years ago so the playlist for that show itself is, say, 56 videos going back to 2022. But in the past 1-3 months you've covered 10 episodes. I'd love a quick and simple way for me to just watch those 10 episodes in a row without having to navigate through the 56 video playlist to try to figure out what i last saw. But I'd still like that full playlist for circumstances where i haven't heard of the topic at all. 

And then if you have ones that are not parts of series, it'd still be super nice to have a quick and easy way to chronologically watch those-- because you'll sometimes reference other unrelated videos in your video and I'll want to watch that first to get a joke or whatever but it can be a whole process trying to figure out which one it was. 

I can only imagine something like I'm describing would probably be annoying af to try to implement and keep up to date. So i do have an alternate thought: 

What if you made mega episode videos where you put multiple of your regular smaller videos in a row chronologically, so someone who wants to binge can either find the videos individually or could choose to play this super long video instead? That way wherever we may need to pause, we still can much more easily figure out where we left off AND we know we aren't missing videos in between. 

Maybe you'd do it like every 10 episodes makes a new mega ep. And you collect the same/similar in their own videos but maybe also do a collage collection basically. 

So i could watch the 10 or whatever latest predator videos in one video, or i could watch the 10 latest bwc cop videos, or i could watch a mega episode of the 10-20 or whatever latest non-chronological random videos in a row without missing anything important. That could also allow you to make sure people don't miss relevant videos to whatever jokes or etc that they otherwise may have skipped thinking it wasn't related to the other video. 

That way you also include longform content versions of your normal videos, which may help attract some people who prefer long videos while also hopefully positively affecting your financial diversity. Especially with YouTube's constantly changing algorithm. 

Nat Geo did a mega episode of 5 of their full episodes in a row from a show they did, and i found that to be incredibly convenient and fun and interesting. It let me put the video on while i was working or doing something else, knowing i wouldn't have to keep jumping over to make sure i wasn't missing videos in between with YouTube's autoplay, AND when i wanted to introduce that show or channel to someone else it was waaayyyy easier having that one link to share to show them what i was talking about than trying to explain to them how to find the specific videos on the channel itself. 

And since you can share a link that starts at a timestamp, you can still direct someone to a specific point in a specific video in that larger compilation. If you were to include the timestamps as jumping chapter points on the video itself that would make it even more useful. 

I don't know if anyone else would agree with me on this-- or, even if anyone does, whether it's even plausible for you guys to implement in the channel without it being a massive time suck that you don't get proper returns on. 

But i do have to say i would personally love that secondary option, letting me watch your individual videos if I'm in the mood for shorter length content or i don't care about missing videos in between or etc-- while also giving me a binge-worthy and binge-ready long form video of multiple of the smaller videos for me to watch all at once, knowing the creator has had a hand and say in the order and videos selected and whatever else that makes it fit the channel or topic or etc best.
